name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,831

entries.clue: Dad's fun paperback to take on holiday? (8)

blocks.note: Pa is Dad, and the clue's own apostrophe-s follows him
sport in the older sense of amusement, as in 'said in sport'

annotation.surface: Wondering whether Dad's paperback is the one to pack for the beach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paperback' points straight at holiday reading, and the booklet it really means is the one without which the holiday never starts. The question mark is the setter admitting the stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: A passport is the paper-covered booklet no trip abroad begins without, so the definition names it by its cover and its use.

entries.clue: Retired president shot Democrat (4)

blocks.note: Abraham Lincoln, the president shot in a Washington theatre, went by Abe
d is the standing short form for a Democrat, as on a US ballot paper

annotation.surface: A news headline: a former president has shot a Democrat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired' means gone to bed for the night, not gone from office, and the headline reading of the clue exists only to keep you in politics. Abe for Lincoln is worth stocking.
annotation.definitionFit: To be abed is to be in bed, which is where you are once you have retired for the night.

entries.clue: Pool and chess diverted playwright (9)

indicatorNotes.diverted: something diverted has been pushed off the course it was set on, and these letters leave the order they arrived in

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

annotation.surface: A games evening of pool and chess sent off somewhere else.
annotation.walkthrough: Two modern games hold an ancient tragedian, and 'diverted' is what re-sets them. Nine letters of fodder fill a nine-letter entry, so nothing is added or dropped on the way.
annotation.definitionFit: Sophocles wrote Antigone and Oedipus Rex for the Athenian stage, which makes him a playwright.

entries.clue: Stop rubbing metal sheet with top scratched (3)

indicatorNotes.scratched: to scratch an entry is to strike it off the list, so the letter named beside it is struck off the word

blocks.note: kitchen foil is a sheet of very thin metal
the top of a down entry is its first letter, and FOIL starts with F

annotation.surface: Being told to stop rubbing a metal sheet whose top has been scratched.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stop rubbing' asks for lubrication, not for someone to keep still. In a down entry the top is the opening letter, which is the one the scratching takes off the metal sheet.
annotation.definitionFit: Oil a hinge and its parts stop rubbing against each other, so the definition names the stuff by the job it does.

entries.clue: Bear and rodents mostly venerated by Native Americans (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly is not quite all of it, so the word beside it arrives one letter short at the end

blocks.note: to tote something is to carry it, which is one sense of bear
mice are rodents, and only most of the word is wanted

annotation.surface: A bear and some mice held in reverence by Native Americans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is the verb here, not the animal the surface parades beside the mice. A totem is the carved emblem a Native American clan takes as its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A totem pole carries the emblems a clan holds sacred, so whatever Native Americans venerate in that way is totemic.

entries.clue: Racer showing expertise after gear twisted (2-4)

indicatorNotes.after: after means behind in an across entry, so the expertise falls in at the back and what the gear supplies leads
indicatorNotes.twisted: a twisted thing has been wrung right round, so the gear's letters are read the other way about

blocks.note: a cog is a toothed gear wheel
art is skill or expertise, as in the art of conversation

annotation.surface: A racing driver showing real skill once the gearbox has been wrenched round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gear' looks like the gearbox of a racing car and is a single toothed wheel. The enumeration 2-4 gives the game away: the answer is a hyphenated compound, not a six-letter word.
annotation.definitionFit: A go-cart is the small low-slung machine raced round a circuit, so 'racer' names it by the one thing it is built for.

entries.clue: Police station, motorway and lake at the bottom of unusual garden (11)

indicatorNotes.at the bottom of: the bottom of a down entry is its far end, so the pieces named before this settle underneath the rest
indicatorNotes.unusual: what is unusual is not in the state you expect it in, and these letters are not in the order you expect either

blocks.note: six letters waiting to be re-set
British motorways are numbered from an M, as in the M1
Erie is one of the Great Lakes, between Ontario and Ohio

annotation.surface: A police station with a motorway and a lake beyond the far end of a strange garden.
annotation.walkthrough: The French keep their gendarmerie as a military police force, and the word covers the barracks as well as the men. 'Lake' wanting a proper name rather than a single letter is the harder half.
annotation.definitionFit: A gendarmerie is both the French police force and the building it operates from, which is a police station.

entries.clue: Open top Ferrari? I would, given a raise (5)

indicatorNotes.given a raise: a raise lifts a thing upward, and lifting letters in a down entry means reading them from the foot of the column

blocks.note: a Ferrari is one make of car, the general word standing in for the particular
I would shortens in speech to I'd

annotation.surface: Saying you would buy a convertible Ferrari if the pay rise came through.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Open top Ferrari' reads as one thing, a convertible, and the parse splits it between definition and wordplay. Cardi is the everyday British shortening of cardigan.
annotation.definitionFit: A cardigan buttons down the front instead of pulling over the head, which makes it the top that opens.

entries.clue: Switch identity wearing jewellery with short hairstyle (6,4)

indicatorNotes.wearing: jewellery sits right round the person wearing it, so what is described as wearing goes on the inside

blocks.note: a ring is the commonest piece of jewellery there is
ID is the standing short form for identity, as on an ID card
a crop is hair cut close to the head

annotation.surface: Swapping identities while got up in jewellery and a close haircut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Switch identity' reads as one phrase and is the trap: switch is the definition, a thin whippy rod, and identity belongs to the wordplay. A riding crop is the short whip carried on horseback.
annotation.definitionFit: A switch is a slender flexible rod used for striking, which is exactly what a rider's crop is.

entries.clue: Italian translated Plato, and Annie (10)

indicatorNotes.translated: to translate is to carry something over into another form, and these letters are carried over into another arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

annotation.surface: An Italian who has put Plato, and then the musical Annie, into his own language.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics mark Annie as the musical, which is what makes it an odd companion for Plato on a translator's desk. 'Italian' is the definition and the whole of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Naples is an Italian city, so a Neapolitan, one of its natives, is an Italian.

entries.clue: The Woman in White, wanting book for trip (4)

indicatorNotes.wanting: to want something is to be short of it, so whatever is named next is missing from the letters

blocks.note: the woman in white at a wedding, and in italics Wilkie Collins's novel as well
b is the standing short form for book

annotation.surface: A woman dressed in white who would sooner have an outing than a novel.
annotation.walkthrough: The italicised title points at Wilkie Collins and at the wedding aisle at once, and only the aisle hands over letters. Trip here is the noun: an outing, not a stumble.
annotation.definitionFit: A ride is a short journey taken in a vehicle or on a horse, which is what a trip out amounts to.

entries.clue: Moral objection against people crossing sea being sent back (12)

indicatorNotes.crossing: to cross something is to cut straight across it, so these letters go in at the join rather than on the end
indicatorNotes.being sent back: something sent back retraces the way it came, and in an across entry that means writing its letters right to left

blocks.note: the con side of an argument is the one against
the Med is what the British call the Mediterranean
a nation is a people considered as one body

annotation.surface: Objecting on moral grounds to people being turned back as they cross the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a live argument about small boats, which is why 'people crossing sea' reads as a single phrase; the parse cuts it in three. Med for Mediterranean is ordinary British speech.
annotation.definitionFit: Condemnation is disapproval expressed on moral grounds, which is what a moral objection amounts to when it is spoken aloud.

entries.clue: Dire actor in cast fixated with theory (11)

indicatorNotes.cast: metal is cast by pouring it into a new shape, so a word told it is cast comes out shaped differently

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eleven letters

annotation.surface: A terrible actor in the company who cannot stop theorising.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as the company of actors and is the shuffle instruction, and 'in' is fodder rather than a container. Someone doctrinaire holds to the theory whatever the facts do.
annotation.definitionFit: A doctrinaire applies a theory rigidly and will not let experience bend it, which is what being fixated with theory looks like.

entries.clue: Patter of light rain in Manchester town? Check (5,5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' is the plainest containment word there is: what is in something sits inside it, here inside the two pieces named after it

blocks.note: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester, south-west of the city centre
when it spits, only a few light drops come down
ch is the chess notation for check

annotation.surface: The sound of drizzle falling on a Manchester suburb.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Patter' is the pitter-patter of rain on the surface and a seller's practised talk in the grid. The question mark flags Sale as one Manchester town among many.
annotation.definitionFit: Patter is the fast rehearsed talk of a salesman or a conjuror, which is precisely what a sales pitch is made of.

entries.clue: First item on list Craig developed a stinker? (6)

indicatorNotes.First item on: the first item on a list is the one at its head, and the head of a word is its opening letter
indicatorNotes.developed: a thing that has developed has grown into a shape it did not have before, and so do these letters

blocks.note: the first letter of list
anagram fodder, five letters

annotation.surface: Craig, top of the list, has turned out to be a stinker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First item on list' looks like more of the story about Craig and is only one letter of it. The question mark excuses the definition: what stinks here is a vegetable, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Garlic's smell clings to the breath for hours, so 'a stinker' names it by the one thing everybody complains of.

entries.clue: Return Spooner's worthless crap (8)

indicatorNotes.Spooner's: the Reverend Spooner is remembered for trading the opening sounds of two words, so say the pair aloud and swap their fronts

blocks.note: a bum deal is a worthless one, and with its partner's opening sound in front it is said the way this is written
cack is British slang for excrement, and with the b it borrows it is said the way this is written

annotation.surface: Spooner dismissing something as worthless rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: Say 'bum cack' and trade the b and the c at the front; the vowel drifts a little on the way, which is normal in a Spoonerism. 'Return' is a noun, so the answer is one too.
annotation.definitionFit: A comeback is a return to the ring, the stage or the charts after a spell away.

entries.clue: Ammunition belt from outlaw desperado emptied with sly look (9)

indicatorNotes.emptied: an emptied vessel keeps nothing but its walls, so the word beside it keeps nothing but its outermost letters

blocks.note: to ban a practice is to outlaw it
the word with everything between its first and last letters taken out
a leer is a sly sidelong look

annotation.surface: A gunbelt taken off a hollow-eyed bandit with a sly expression.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' is the verb, so the desperado beside it is not his partner in the story but a word to be hollowed out. A bandoleer is the cartridge belt slung across the chest.
annotation.definitionFit: A bandoleer is the shoulder belt fitted with loops for cartridges, so 'ammunition belt' is its plain description.

entries.clue: Careful, certainly, spiking sweet drink with alcohol (8)

indicatorNotes.spiking: to spike a drink is to slip something into it unnoticed, and that is what happens to these letters

blocks.note: mead is fermented honey, sweet and alcoholic, the oldest drink in the country
sure means certainly, as in 'sure, I'll come'

annotation.surface: Someone careful who is certainly slipping something stronger into a sweet drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The spiking in the story and the spiking in the parse are the same act, which is what makes the surface sit so still. Measured means deliberate and unhurried, as in a measured response.
annotation.definitionFit: A measured response is a careful one, weighed out before it is given rather than blurted.

entries.clue: Desperate religious festival with cross upside-down (2-2-3)

indicatorNotes.upside-down: turned upside-down, a down entry's letters are read from the foot of the column back up to the top

blocks.note: Eid is the Muslim festival marking the end of Ramadan
a rood is the crucifix set above the screen of an old English church

annotation.surface: A religious festival kept with the cross hung the wrong way up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is the noun, and it is the old English word for it that the grid wants. Upside-down is precise rather than decorative: this is a down entry, so the pair is read up the column.
annotation.definitionFit: A do-or-die attempt is made in desperation, with nothing held back and no second chance to come.

entries.clue: Irregular headed up military department after revolution (6)

indicatorNotes.revolution: a revolution carries a thing right round, so what it acts on ends up facing the other way

blocks.note: to head up a department is to run it, so headed up is ran
the MoD is the Ministry of Defence, the British government department in charge of the armed forces

annotation.surface: An irregular soldier who ran the defence ministry after the coup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Headed up' looks like an instruction to lift letters and is only the past tense of run. The surface's revolution is a coup; the wordplay's is a half-turn.
annotation.definitionFit: Something random follows no rule or pattern, so it is irregular in the sense of unpredictable rather than unlawful.

entries.clue: Cheat adjusted the scoreboard at change of ends? (3,3,4,2)

annotation.definition2: adjusted the scoreboard at change of ends

blocks.note: the idiom for getting the better of someone by trickery

blocks.clueFragment: adjusted the scoreboard at change of ends
blocks.note: in cricket the bowling switches ends after every over, and the scorer's job then is to add that over to the board

annotation.surface: A scorer quietly fiddling the board while the teams swap ends.
annotation.walkthrough: The cricket reading needs the phrase re-split, with 'one over' as the six balls just bowled and 'on' pointing at the board. 'Cheat' is the definition, sitting alone at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: To put one over on somebody is to cheat them; read as cricket, each change of ends is a scorer putting one more over on the board.

entries.clue: Tariff applied to biological category (5)

blocks.note: a tariff is a tax charged on imported goods
a duty applied to something is a duty on it

annotation.surface: A tariff charged on a category of living things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Applied to' is not joinery: it is the two letters that finish the word. A taxon is any named rank in the classification of living things, from species up to kingdom.
annotation.definitionFit: A taxon is any named group in biological classification, which is what a biological category is.

entries.clue: Drug charity stocks a bit of cannabis (4)

indicatorNotes.stocks: a shop stocks goods by holding them inside, so the word here closes round what comes next
indicatorNotes.a bit of: a bit of a word is a piece broken off it, and the piece a word offers first is its opening letter

blocks.note: aid is charity in the form of practical help
the opening letter of cannabis

annotation.surface: A drugs charity that keeps a little cannabis in stock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drug' looks like the start of a sentence about a charity and is the definition standing on its own. Aid for charity is common currency in these puzzles.
annotation.definitionFit: Acid is the street name for LSD, which makes 'drug' its plainest classification.

entries.clue: Greek river becomes blocked, by the sound of it (4)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: judging a word by the sound of it means taking what you hear rather than what is written

blocks.note: a drawer that becomes blocked sticks

annotation.surface: A Greek river that seems to be silting up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Becomes blocked' is the word you say aloud, and the spelling it lands on is Greek rather than English. The Styx is the river the dead were ferried across in myth.
annotation.definitionFit: The Styx is the river of the Greek underworld, the one Charon ferried the dead across.

entries.clue: Dotty lending cue as favour (10)

indicatorNotes.Dotty: someone dotty is not in their right mind, and these letters are not in their right order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

annotation.surface: Dotty is lending out her snooker cue as a favour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' reads as a woman's name at the head of the sentence and is the shuffle instruction. An indulgence is a favour granted, and in the medieval Church a remission of penance bought for cash.
annotation.definitionFit: An indulgence is a favour or concession granted to someone, the noun behind indulging a child's request.

entries.clue: Shown key turns (3)

indicatorNotes.turns: a thing that turns comes round to face the other way, so its letters are taken in the opposite order

blocks.note: Del is the delete key on a computer keyboard

annotation.surface: Being shown how the key turns.
annotation.walkthrough: The key is a keyboard's, not a door's, and that swap is the whole of this three-letter clue. 'Shown' is past tense, so the answer is too: led to your seat, shown to your seat.
annotation.definitionFit: Led and shown are interchangeable for an usher's work: you are led to your table, or shown to it.

entries.clue: Novelty exhibit in church (6)

indicatorNotes.in: what is in something sits inside it, so the piece named first goes within the piece named last

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England, the standing short form for church
a gallery hangs a painting when it puts it on show

annotation.surface: A novelty exhibit on show inside a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exhibit' is the verb, not the object exhibited, and the whole surface rests on reading it the other way. A change is a novelty in the sense of doing something for a change.
annotation.definitionFit: A change is something different from the usual, which is what novelty means in 'let's have fish for a change'.

entries.clue: The Spanish explorer ultimately disappointed over this quest? (8)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: what comes ultimately is what comes last, so the word beside it gives up only its final letter

blocks.note: el is the Spanish word for 'the'
Dora the Explorer is the map-carrying heroine of the children's cartoon
the last letter of disappointed
o is the cricket scorer's short form for an over

annotation.surface: A Spanish explorer left disappointed at the end of this search.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The Spanish' is not a nationality here but the Spanish word for 'the', and the explorer beside it is a cartoon child with a backpack rather than a conquistador. Over is the cricketer's O.
annotation.definitionFit: Eldorado is the golden city the conquistadors searched South America for and never found, so the name stands for the search as much as the place.
